changes.how: In `cronJobs` (the table "cron_jobs", line 16791 today) add three columns: `worked: integer("worked").notNull().default(0)` (runs that took at least one item), `lastWorkedAt: timestamp("last_worked_at", { withTimezone: true })`, `budgetMs: integer("budget_ms")` (nullable). Then a custom migration `pnpm exec drizzle-kit generate --custom --name cron_retired_jobs` with one statement: `delete from commerce.cron_jobs where job = 'dispatcher.content-reports';`, then `node scripts/prune-snapshots.mjs`.

(1) Add an exported pure `workedOf(result: unknown): boolean`: true when result is a number above 0, or an array with length above 0, or an object in which any own value is a number above 0, a non-empty array, or (one level down) an object for which workedOf is true; false for null, undefined, 0, false and empty shapes. (2) record() gains two parameters, `worked: boolean` and `budgetMs: number | null`; the insert adds the columns worked (1 or 0), last_worked_at (the finish time when worked, else null) and budget_ms; the `on conflict` adds `worked = j.worked + excluded.worked, last_worked_at = coalesce(excluded.last_worked_at, j.last_worked_at), budget_ms = excluded.budget_ms`. (3) tracked() passes workedOf(result) on success and false on failure; it gains an optional fourth parameter `options?: { budgetMs?: number }`. (4) cronJobRows(): select also last_duration_ms, worked, last_worked_at, budget_ms and filter retired names in the query (`where job <> all(${textList(RETIRED_JOBS)})`); in runJobs() delete the block that deletes RETIRED_JOBS rows on every run (the migration removed the one retired row). Keep everything step 0.45 and step 1.26 put in runJobs() (the pool of four, the 60 s lane rule, report).

CronJobRow gains `lastDurationMs: number | null; worked: number; runs: number; lastWorkedAt: string | null; budgetMs: number | null`. CronHealth becomes "ok" | "late" | "failing" | "slow". cronHealth(): after the failing and late tests, return "slow" when row.budgetMs is a number and row.lastDurationMs is a number above it. jobsNeedingLook() sorts failing first, then late, then slow. Add the pure `jobDue(every: number, lastStartedAt: string | null, now: Date): boolean`: every 300 is always due; 3,600 is due when lastStartedAt is null or before the start of now's UTC hour; 86,400 when null or before the start of now's UTC day.

The page already reads cronJobRows() (line 41). In its jobs table add three columns per job: Runs, Worked, Last worked (a relative time, or a dash when null), and one more, Idle runs a day. Idle runs a day comes from the daily reading of step 1.13 if that reading stores each ledger row's runs (find it: rg -n 'cron_jobs' src/server -g '!*.test.ts' | rg -i 'reading|daily|snapshot'): extend that reading to store worked too and show (runs today minus runs yesterday) minus (worked today minus worked yesterday). New column titles are admin text: add them in English and Norwegian to the area this page's words come from (the page shows which area it reads), in the way that area's other titles are written.

Add: jobDue for 300, 3,600 and 86,400 at 12:04:59 with a last start at 11:59, 12:00:10 and yesterday; allowances for 3,600 (late after three hours) and 86,400 (thirty hours); a row with budgetMs 5,000 and lastDurationMs 9,000 is slow, with failures 3 it is failing, with no finished run it is late.

commits.title: The dispatcher runs from a registry: each job has a cadence, a reason, a growth label and a budget

changes.how: Add the registry's types: `export type JobEvery = 300 | 3600 | 86400; export type JobWork = "set" | { perStore: { cap: number; order: string } }; export type RegistryJob<T = unknown> = { every: JobEvery; why: string; work: JobWork; budgetMs: number; run: (report: (error: unknown) => void) => Promise<T>; after?: (result: T) => void };` (match the exact `report` type step 1.26 gave jobs). Add `runRegistry(prefix, registry, options?: { now?: () => number; runBudgetMs?: number })` beside runJobs(); runJobs() stays for other callers until step 3.4. runRegistry does, in order: (a) ONE read: `select job, last_started_at from commerce.cron_jobs where job like ${prefix + '.%'}` through typedRows(); (b) due = the jobs for which jobDue(every, lastStartedAt, now) is true; a job that is not due is not run and not recorded, and its row stays; (c) order: jobs with budgetMs up to 10,000 first in registry order, then the rest by rising budget; (d) the pool of four from step 0.45; before starting a job test `elapsed + job.budgetMs <= runBudgetMs` where runBudgetMs defaults to 240,000: a job whose budget does not fit is not started (it is due again next tick; log `cron.job_not_started` with the job and the milliseconds left, through log()); so no job starts after 240 s; (e) after a job ends call its `after(result)` at once (the cache refreshes that today wait for all jobs), inside a try that logs; (f) ledger: a job that failed, or whose result workedOf() is true, is recorded at once with record() as today (its record survives a killed function); every other finished job (idle) is collected and written at the end in ONE statement, a multi-row `insert into commerce.cron_jobs ... values (...), (...) on conflict (job) do update` with the same set-list record() uses, worked 0; (g) return the same shape runJobs() returns (name to result or null).

Turn the object passed to runJobs("dispatcher", EVERY, {...}) (line 127 today) into `const JOBS = { ... } satisfies Record<string, RegistryJob>` and call `runRegistry("dispatcher", JOBS)`. Each entry keeps its key and its call exactly, and gains every, why, work and budgetMs. The key `uiTranslations` keeps the literal text `run: () => runNightlyUiTranslations()` on one line. CADENCES. Daily (86400): searches, cache, forms, docsCounts, recommendations, replications. Hourly (3600): apiIdempotency, oauthTokens, chat, houseCustomers, platformBriefing, summaries, analyticsAlerts, reportEmails, autopilotReports, autopilotBudgets, uiTranslations, legalUpkeep, legalSources, businessChanges, recurring, autoArchive, instagram, autopilotEffects, experiments, embeddings, and the new platformPayouts of the next commit. Every other key stays 300, and `trials` MUST stay 300 (settleTrials() is the only caller of reopenAfterPlan(), src/server/store-trial.ts). That leaves 57 keys at 300. WHY: one line per job; take it from the comment that sits above the key today and from the job's rule (for an hourly or daily job say what unit its work is counted in: 'retention is counted in days', 'sent once a store day'). BUDGETS in ms: sms 120000 and legalWrites 120000 (their own deadlines, lines 195 and 246 today); tripletex, fiken, ledger, pipedrive 40000; platformBooks 30000; every other job 5000 unless its own code has a longer deadline constant (read each `run*`'s options for a budget or deadline and use that figure). The sum of all budgets must be 960,000 or less (four lanes of 240 s); if it is not, stop. WORK: 'set' when the job's idle path is a fixed number of statements; `{ perStore: { cap, order } }` when it loops over stores, books or connections, with the cap (stores or seconds a run) and the order it takes them in, read from its code. Known per-store jobs: tripletex, fiken, ledger, autoArchive, autopilotBudgets, recurring, ebay, instagram, knowledge, media, altTexts, embeddings, calendars. Move the five trailing tracked() jobs (lines 262 to 275: themeUpdates, platformThemeUpdates, themePurchases, domainPurchases, domainRegistrations) into JOBS with every 300, and move each revalidateTag that follows a job today into that job's `after`: schedules (pagesTag per store and designTags per theme store), status (STATUS_TAG when measured > 0), themeUpdates (designTags per store), platformThemeUpdates (PLATFORM_NAVIGATION_TAG, PAGES_TAG, DESIGNS_TAG when updated > 0), altTexts (pagesTag and catalogTag per owner). The JSON answer keeps its keys; a job that did not run this tick answers null. Replace the 4,212-character comment above run() (lines 94 to 116) by three lines that point at JOBS. Keep maxDuration = 300 and the outer tracked("route.cart-reminders", EVERY, ...).

Remove the by-hand hourly guard near line 44 (a test that the minute is below 5, which returns early): the registry runs the job hourly. Do the same in src/server/experiment-jobs.ts near line 50, and in src/server/embeddings.ts if step 0.28 added a minute guard to refreshEmbeddings() (rg -n 'getUTCMinutes' src/server/autopilot-effects.ts src/server/experiment-jobs.ts src/server/embeddings.ts). Update each file's own test where it set the clock to pass the guard.

Read the dispatcher's source and parse JOBS by text. New cases: every key of JOBS has `every:` with 300, 3600 or 86400, a non-empty `why:`, a `work:` and a `budgetMs:`; an entry with `perStore` has a `cap` and an `order`; the sum of every `budgetMs` number is 960000 or less; the file calls no `tracked("dispatcher.` outside runRegistry (the trailing jobs are in). Change the existing expectation at line 43 from /uiTranslations: \(\) => runNightlyUiTranslations\(\)/ to a pattern that finds `runNightlyUiTranslations()` inside the uiTranslations entry. Add a fixture case: a small source string with one entry that has no `every` fails the same parser.

A unit test of runRegistry() with the database mocked the way step 0.45's unit test of runJobs() mocks it (reuse that file if 0.45 made one under this name: then add to it). Cases: a job starts only if its budget fits (with a fake clock at 230 s, a 5,000 ms job starts and a 40,000 ms job does not); no job starts after 240 s; never more than four run at once; an hourly job whose ledger start is in this hour is not run; a job's after() runs before a slower job ends; idle jobs are written in one statement and a job that worked in its own; a job that throws leaves the others' rows and is recorded failed.

Made by step 1.10; if missing, stop; do not overwrite.
